rows.jp: 「前の学校で、友達なんていませんでしたから。兄にも私にも」
rows.en: "At our old school, neither my brother nor I had any friends."

ghs.en: Kiri: "Because, at our previous school we did not have friends. Neither I nor Ani."

rows.jp: 「友達だった人にも、裏切られて……誰も信用できなくなって……」
rows.en: “Even people who had been our friends betrayed us... We stopped trusting anyone...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Even the people who were friends betrayed us... we could no longer trust anyone..."

rows.jp: 「誰も傷つけてないのに、みんなから傷つけられて」
rows.en: "We never hurt anyone, but everyone hurt us."

ghs.en: Kiri: "We did not hurt anyone, but still everybody hurt us."

rows.jp: 「けど身を守った猛獣は、撃ち殺されるのが世の常なんだよ」
rows.en: “But that’s the way of the world: any wild beast that defends itself gets shot dead.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But in this world, it's ordinary for wild beasts that defend themselves to be shot to death."

rows.jp: 「世界が恐くてたまらない、です」
rows.en: "I'm so frightened of the world I can't stand it."

ghs.en: Kiri: "The world is unbearably frightening, yes."

ghs.assessment: Kiri identifies everyone's malice as what frightens her. The English instead directly characterizes every person as malicious.

rows.jp: 「……人間なんて、なくなる時にはあっさりなくなるって思ってます……だって、世界にはほとんど何もないから……」
rows.en: “...I think humanity could vanish with astonishing ease when its time comes... because there is almost nothing in the world...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...I think that humans, when they depart, will just vanish like that... because in this world there is nearly nothing."

rows.jp: 「きっと『何もない』方が多いんです。『なにかある』方は、ちょっとだけなんです！」
rows.en: "There must be more 'nothing' than 'something.' 'Something' is only a tiny part!"

ghs.en: Kiri: "I am sure, there is Nothing in so much. In just so little is there Anything!"

rows.jp: 「いつ押し流されてしまうかもわからないって……思って」
rows.en: "I keep thinking we could be swept away at any moment..."

ghs.en: Kiri: "And we won't know when we will be washed away... I think."

rows.jp: 「その……ＳＦみたいな、人類滅亡とか？」
rows.en: “You mean... like humanity going extinct in some sci-fi story?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Sort of... an SF-like thing, the Fall of Mankind?"

rows.jp: 「そういうのとは違って……そういう理由があるのとは違って……」
rows.en: “It isn’t like that... It’s not as if there’d be some reason behind it...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "It is different from that... it is different in how there is a reason in that..."
Kiri: "This will be like waking up from a dream."
ghs.assessment: Kiri makes an atemporal comparison to waking from a dream. The English invents a future event and an explicit subject.

rows.jp: 「いがみあってばかりで、こわいだけなのに……」
rows.en: "All people do is fight, and it's frightening enough already..."

ghs.en: Kiri: "If all is quarreling, then everything is scary..."
ghs.assessment: Kiri says people do nothing but quarrel and that this is merely frightening. The English changes the statement into an ungrammatical conditional.
ghs.remedy: All people do is quarrel, and it's only frightening...

highlights.text: If all is quarreling, then everything is scary

rows.jp: 「けどある日、突然すべてがなくなって……ちっぽけな世界で……もし自分ひとりが取り残されたらって考えると……」
rows.en: "But then one day everything suddenly disappears... and in that tiny world... if I were the only one left behind..."

ghs.en: Kiri: "But one day, all of a sudden everything will be no more... and I keep thinking, what if I was the only one that will be left behind... in that tiny worthless world..."

rows.jp: 「幸せの形が、人と違うだけさ」
rows.en: “It’s just that happiness takes a different shape for everyone.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The shape happiness takes is different among people, that's all."

ghs.assessment: Kiri says she does not want or cannot bear that kind of existence. The English recasts her aversion as a moral judgment that it is incorrect.

rows.jp: 「悪意はないのかもしれないけれど、わたしはそんなのはいやです」
rows.en: "There may be no malice, but I don't want that."

ghs.en: Kiri: "There might not be malice or anything, but, that is not right to me."
ghs.assessment: Kiri says that even if there is no malice, she still hates or rejects such a state. The English turns her emotional refusal into a claim about correctness.

highlights.text: that is not right to me

rows.jp: 「だって……人がいるのに……一人一人が絶海の孤島みたいで……閉じてて……」
rows.en: "Because... even though people are there... each one is like a lonely island in the open sea... closed off..."

ghs.en: Kiri: "Because... when people exist... to still exist one by one as if solitary islands on distant seas... closed off..."

rows.en: It was as if Kiri were—

rows.jp: そう叫んでいるように見えた。

ghs.assessment: The Japanese narrates the transition of waking up. The English gives a past state of already being awake.

rows.en: A conversation with Kiri about malice.

ghs.en: That chat with Kiri about malice.

rows.jp: そういえば二人が、どう世界から拒絶されていたのか、俺は知らない。
rows.en: Come to think of it, I did not know how the world had rejected the two of them.

ghs.en: Which reminds me that I didn't know in what way, exactly, those two had been rejected from the world.
ghs.assessment: The narrator says he still does not know exactly how the two were rejected by the world. The English confines that lack of knowledge to the past.

rows.jp: だいたいは想像はつくけれど。
rows.en: I could imagine most of it.

ghs.en: The rough outline is imaginable, however.

rows.jp: 結局人は、自分のために生きている。
rows.en: In the end, people live for themselves.

ghs.en: In the end, people are living for their own sake.

rows.jp: 人と触れあうことで生じる、様々な欲望の中で。
rows.en: Among all the desires born from contact with other people.

ghs.en: In the midst of so many desires produced by a meeting of touches with other people.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese refers to interacting or coming into contact with other people. The English calques the components into a physically incoherent 'meeting of touches.'

highlights.text: a meeting of touches with other people

rows.jp: ほどよい時間になっていた。

ghs.en: The time was now just right.

rows.jp: フェンスから外界を見渡している。
rows.en: She was looking out through the fence at the world beyond.

rows.jp: 既視感が、俺の意識を過去昔へと連れ去った。
rows.en: Déjà vu swept my mind back into the distant past.

rows.jp: 夏も終わりかけていた。
蝉たちも一際うるさい。
rows.en: The cicadas were louder than ever.

rows.jp: 叩きつけるような鳴き声。
最後の命を振り絞っていると知れる。
rows.en: You could hear them wringing out the last of their lives.

rows.jp: 命の残滓に彩られる夏。
rows.en: Summer, painted with the residue of life.

ghs.en: It was a Summer tinged in the dregs of life.

rows.jp: 背後からでも、肩の震えを見ればわかる。
rows.en: Even from behind, I could tell by the trembling of her shoulders.

ghs.en: Even from the back, that shaking of the shoulders is unmistakable.

rows.en: She made no attempt to hide her tears.

ghs.en: She does not hide her tears.
Kiri: "Yutaka... Yutaka, he... fell from here..."

ghs.assessment: The first-person narrator says that he knew. The English changes the subject to Kiri.

rows.jp: 知らない者はいなかった。

ghs.en: There was no one who didn't,

rows.jp: 世間一般では、学生が一人飛び降り自殺をすれば、それなりに話題になる。
rows.en: Ordinarily, when a student jumped to their death, it caused something of a stir.

ghs.en: In society at large, a student leaping off to his death on his own would be newsworthy, in some way.

rows.jp: 保護者は学校を問いつめ、誰が悪いのか、白日のもとにさらそうとする。
rows.en: Parents pressed the school for answers, trying to drag the guilty party into the light of day.

ghs.en: Guardians would press the school with questions, so as to bring to daylight who was in the wrong.

rows.jp: 学校も責任を回避しようとする。
rows.en: The school tried to evade responsibility.

ghs.en: And the school, then, would try to avoid responsibility.

rows.en: None of that happened at Gunjo.

ghs.en: But at Gunjou there is none of that.

rows.jp: 世間の誰も問いつめてはこないし、学校も逃げない。
rows.en: No one from the outside came demanding answers, and the school did not shirk.

ghs.en: No one in society would press questions, and the school would not dodge them.

rows.jp: 何人かの人間が責任を取った。
世間は群青の危険な少年少女たちのことなど、どうでも良かった。
rows.en: The world did not care what happened to Gunjo's dangerous boys and girls.

ghs.en: To the world, the dangerous boys and girls of Gunjou and all that is around them could do whatever they wanted with themselves.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the wider world did not care about Gunjou's dangerous boys and girls. The English instead says the students and their surroundings could do whatever they wanted with themselves.

highlights.text: To the world, the dangerous boys and girls of Gunjou and all that is around them could do whatever they wanted with themselves.

rows.jp: 「誰も……誰も……悲しまない……わたしたちがどういう気持ちで……生きてきたのか……誰もっ」
rows.en: “No one... no one is grieving... No one cares how we felt... how we've lived... No one!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "No one... no one... is even sad... for all the feelings that we had lived with... no one!"
There was a rare excitement here.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says Kiri was unusually agitated. The English removes her as subject and turns her state into an unidentified excitement in a place.

highlights.text: There was a rare excitement here.

rows.jp: 豊の死から、すでに一週間が経過していた。
rows.en: A full week had already passed since Yutaka's death.

ghs.en: One week had already passed since Yutaka's death.

rows.jp: 霧の悲嘆は遅れてきていた。

ghs.en: Kiri's grief had come behind schedule.

rows.jp: 「なあ霧……豊は、幸せだったのかな」
rows.en: “Kiri... do you think Yutaka was happy?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Say, Kiri, I'm wondering... was Yutaka happy?"

rows.jp: 「あいつはあいつなりに、幸せだったのかな？」
rows.en: “Do you think he was happy in his own way?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'm wondering, was that guy happy, even in his own way?"

ghs.assessment: 'Usual' begins with a consonant sound and takes 'a,' not 'an.'

rows.jp: 意味はまったく逆だった。

ghs.en: the meaning was wholly and damnably the opposite.

rows.jp: 「……ずっと、つらい思いをしてきたんです」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...always, he was always feeling bitter."
ghs.assessment: Kiri says Yutaka had been suffering or enduring painful experiences. 'Feeling bitter' instead suggests resentment.

rows.jp: 「一瞬でも、幸せな時間はなかった？」
rows.en: “Wasn't there even one moment when he was happy?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "There were never times of happiness, not even one instant?"

rows.jp: 「……先輩と友達になってからは……笑うように……」
rows.en: “...After he became friends with you... he started to smile...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...since he became friends with you, Senpai... he seemed to be smiling..."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese address is left as an unexplained honorific, and 笑うように means he began or came to smile after becoming friends with Taichi, not merely that he seemed to be smiling.

highlights.text: you, Senpai... he seemed to be smiling

rows.jp: 「けど全然取り戻してないっ」
rows.en: “But he never got any of it back!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "But he did not recover in the slightest!"

rows.jp: 「受けた苦しみを、ちっとも取り戻してないっ」
rows.en: “It didn't come close to making up for all the suffering he endured!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "He didn't recover at all, not from all the anguish he had suffered!"
ghs.assessment: Kiri says that none of the suffering inflicted on him had been made up for or restored to him. The English instead says that he personally failed to recover from anguish.

highlights.text: He didn't recover at all, not from all the anguish he had suffered!

rows.jp: 「じゃあ霧ちんは、豊の人生が取るに足らないものだったと思ってるわけか」
rows.en: “So you think Yutaka's life amounted to nothing, Kiri-kins?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Therefore, Kiri-chin, you think that the life Yutaka was living had no value, do you?"
ghs.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address is left unexplained rather than represented in English.

rows.jp: 「……と言ってはみたものの、悲しいのは理屈じゃないものな」
rows.en: “...Though even as I say that, grief isn't rational.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...so I might say, however, sadness is not something rational."
ghs.assessment: と言ってはみたものの means 'that said' or 'although I say that.' The English sequence does not form the intended concessive relation idiomatically.

rows.en: About what should be done with Kiri.

ghs.en: as to how to treat Kiri.

rows.en: I looked up at the sky.

ghs.en: I look up at the sky.

rows.jp: 視界を埋めた純白が、巨大な入道雲と理解できるまでの刹那。
rows.en: For an instant, pure white filled my vision before resolving into a vast thunderhead.

ghs.en: An instant passed before I could understand that the pure white my vision was buried in was an enormous cluster of cumulonimbus.
ghs.assessment: 入道雲 refers to one enormous towering cumulonimbus cloud. 'Cumulonimbus' is being used as a mass/category noun after 'cluster of' rather than naming that cloud.

rows.jp: 蝉たちの最期とともに。
rows.en: Along with the cicadas' final hours.

ghs.en: Along with the last moments of the cicadas' lives.

rows.jp: 万感こもごも含んだ意味に、霧には聞こえたのだろう。
rows.en: Kiri must have heard those words as freighted with every imaginable emotion.

ghs.en: Kiri must have heard thousands of feelings within that meaning, one after the other.
ghs.assessment: 万感こもごも means the words carried a whole mixture or flood of emotions. The English literalizes 万 as an exact count and turns simultaneous mixed feeling into a temporal sequence.

highlights.text: thousands of feelings within that meaning, one after the other

rows.jp: 「……うわぁぁぁぁぁぁぁぁぁぁぁぁぁ！」
目を伏せ、俺のシャツの裾を掴んで、声を張り上げた。
rows.en: She lowered her eyes, seized the hem of my shirt, and wailed.

ghs.en: Eyes downcast, grabbing the hem of my shirt, and screaming out.

rows.jp: 「ゆたにぃが……死んじゃった……死んで……」

ghs.assessment: The intimate older-brother address is reproduced in Japanese morphology without an English representation.

rows.jp: 大好きな、お兄ちゃんだったわけだ。
rows.en: The big brother she had loved so dearly.

ghs.en: He was her beloved onii-chan, that's what he was.
ghs.assessment: お兄ちゃん identifies her beloved older brother in an affectionate register. The English leaves the kinship term and suffix untranslated.

rows.jp: 片足でも立派に生きて。
rows.en: He had lived admirably, even with one leg.

ghs.en: Living magnificently even if on one leg.

rows.jp: 豊の葬式で見た二人の顔には、軽い安堵があった。
rows.en: On both their faces at Yutaka’s funeral, I’d seen a hint of relief.

rows.jp: 霧はそのことに気づいているのか？
おそらく、悟っているに違いなかった。
いろんなつらい目に遭っても、二人で支え合ってきたんだろう。
rows.en: However much they suffered, the two of them must have supported each other.
He had been her other half.

ghs.en: Kiri is only an half, yes.
ghs.assessment: 'Half' begins with a consonant sound and takes 'a,' not 'an.'

rows.jp: ただ霧は、望んでそうなった。
rows.en: Only Kiri had chosen to become that way.

ghs.en: Except Kiri seemed to have wished for that.
ghs.assessment: 望んでそうなった says that Kiri became that way because she wanted or chose it. The English misreads そうなった as evidential 'seemed' and reduces the deliberate result to a past wish.

highlights.text: seemed to have wished for that

rows.jp: 今は強い感情が気力を剥奪している。
rows.en: For now, powerful emotion had stripped away her strength.

ghs.en: Right now, strong emotions are depriving her of vigor.

rows.jp: が、いずれ悲しみが薄れれば、あるべきはずのもう半分を求めるだろう。
rows.en: But once her grief faded, she would seek the other half that ought to have been there.

ghs.en: But should someday the sadness grow faint, she will be searching for that half that she expects to be there, that must be there.
ghs.assessment: The inverted conditional places 'someday' between the modal and subject in a non-English order.

highlights.text: should someday the sadness grow faint

rows.en: Two people who had been one body and soul.

ghs.assessment: 一心同体 describes two people united in mind and body or functioning as one. 'Alter egos' means alternative selves or personae and does not express their mutual unity.
罪はない here means Kiri is not at fault or is innocent. 'Has no sin' imposes an unnatural religious formulation.

rows.jp: けど俺は……俺の怪物は、身じろぎしてしまった。

ghs.en: but I... my monster was already stirring.

rows.en: I put an arm around her back.

ghs.assessment: The first-person narrator says he puts an arm or his hands around her back. The English removes him as agent and describes unidentified hands moving on her.

rows.jp: 激情が索敵を甘くして、霧は気づかない。
rows.en: Her grief had blunted her vigilance. She did not notice.

ghs.en: Violent emotions make enemy warning mechanisms less sharp, and Kiri does not notice.

rows.jp: 少しずつ、情緒は沈静化していく。
rows.en: Little by little, her emotions settled.

ghs.en: Little by little, her emotions were transforming into calmness.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says her emotions gradually settle down. The English changes the state into a transformation toward an abstract noun and unnecessarily shifts into past progressive.

rows.jp: その頃には、俺はすっかり霧を抱きしめていた。
rows.en: By then, I had my arms wrapped all the way around Kiri.

ghs.en: By then, I had completely hugged Kiri.
ghs.assessment: すっかり here means that by then he was fully holding her in an embrace. 'Completely hugged' incorrectly modifies the completed act by degree.
The dialogue opens with a double quotation mark but closes with a single quotation mark.

ghs.en: Taichi: "I am empty. So very much."

rows.jp: 見下ろせば小さな面差し。
rows.en: I looked down at her small face.

ghs.en: If I look down those small features of hers,
ghs.assessment: The Japanese is a descriptive fragment centered on the small face below him. The English creates an unfinished conditional and lacks the required preposition 'at' after 'look down.'

highlights.text: If I look down those small features of hers,

rows.jp: 深みをたたえた黒曜石がふたつ、表面を薄い塩水で濡らす。
rows.en: Two fathomless obsidian eyes, filmed with salt water.

ghs.en: I can see a pair of obsidian stones, full with sadness to the depths, moistening her face with thin salty water.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese likens her two deep eyes to obsidian and says a thin layer of salt water wets their surfaces. The English adds sadness, then makes the stones actively moisten her whole face, reversing what is wetting what.

highlights.text: I can see a pair of obsidian stones, full with sadness to the depths, moistening her face with thin salty water.

rows.jp: 「豊は幸せだったと思うよ。霧もいたし、イヤなことは忘れてたし」
rows.en: “I think Yutaka was happy. He had you, and he'd forgotten all the bad things.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I think Yutaka was happy, you know. Because you were there too, Kiri, so he could forget about the bad things."

rows.jp: 「最期まで、幸せだったって、俺は思ってる」
rows.en: “I think he was happy right up to the end.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "He was happy until his last, that's what I believe."

ghs.assessment: The narrator brings his own face closer to Kiri. The English makes him move her face instead.

rows.jp: 顔を交差するように重ねて。
rows.en: I angled my face over hers.
And took a kiss from her.
I tightened my arms around her.

ghs.assessment: 強く抱きしめた means held or embraced her tightly. 'Hugged with strength' is not idiomatic English.
霧の息が詰まった says Kiri's breath caught or stopped. The English instead says her ongoing breathing became difficult and also omits the possessive apostrophe.

rows.jp: フェンスに押しつけて、唇を吸い続ける。
rows.en: I pinned her against the fence and kept sucking at her lips.

ghs.en: Pushing her against the fence, I continue to suck her lips.
ghs.assessment: In this context 唇を吸う describes continuing the kiss. 'Suck her lips' is distractingly anatomical and nonidiomatic in English.

rows.jp: 驚きが、霧の思考力を奪っていた。
rows.en: Shock had robbed Kiri of the ability to think.

ghs.en: The surprise had stripped Kiri of the ability to think.

rows.en: Shock left her barely able to resist.

ghs.assessment: わからない here is 'I don't know' in answer to whether she is lonely. 'Don't get it' instead suggests failure to understand the question.

rows.jp: 今度は歯茎の内側に、侵略していく。
rows.en: This time, I invaded the space behind her teeth.

ghs.en: This time I go invade the inside of the teethridge.
ghs.assessment: 歯茎 means the gums. 'Teethridge' is not the standard anatomical term and is presented as a closed compound not recognized in English.

rows.jp: 同時に手を、スカートの中に。
rows.en: At the same time, I put a hand under her skirt.

ghs.en: And at the same time, my hands go inside her skirt.

rows.jp: 突如として抵抗が強まる。
俺は薄笑いを浮かべていたんだと思う。きっと。
rows.en: I think I was smirking. I must have been.

ghs.en: I think I am making a faint smile. Definitely.
ghs.assessment: The narrator retrospectively thinks he must have been wearing a faint smile. The English switches to present progressive and sets tentative 'I think' against an independent assertion of certainty.

highlights.text: I think I am making a faint smile. Definitely.

rows.jp: 衝撃が、ゆっくりと嫌悪に覆われていく様を、俺は見ていた。
rows.en: I watched as disgust slowly overtook her shock.

ghs.en: I could see how the the shock was slowing being covered up by disgust.
ghs.assessment: The article is duplicated, and the adverb modifying 'being covered' must be 'slowly,' not 'slowing.'
The Japanese says she passes by Taichi's side. 'Underarm' names the armpit or a throwing style and lacks the possessive needed even for a literal body reference.

rows.en: A creaking door. A closing door.

ghs.assessment: The source presents two beats: the door creaks, then the door closes. The English omits the closing beat entirely.

rows.en: I covered my face with one hand.

rows.jp: なるほど確かにこれはマズイ。
rows.en: I see. Yes, this was bad.

rows.jp: 口元が酷薄に吊り上がっていた。
rows.en: The corners of my mouth had curled upward in a cruel smile.

ghs.en: I ended up estranged from Kiri.

rows.jp: 部活にもあまり顔を出さなくなった。
rows.en: She rarely showed her face at the club anymore.

ghs.en: She nearly stopped showing face at club.

rows.jp: 美希が強引に連れてくることはあったが、俺のことは避けた。
rows.en: Miki sometimes dragged her there, but she avoided me.

ghs.en: There were times when Miki would forcibly bring her along, but she avoided me.

rows.jp: 会話もなくなり、関係は途絶した。
rows.en: We stopped speaking, and the relationship was severed.

rows.jp: そんなことが、あったんだ―――

ghs.en: And that... was one of the things that did happen---

rows.jp: はからずも霧の予言は当たることになった。
rows.en: Kiri's prediction had come true without her intending it.

ghs.en: Unexpectedly, Kiri's guess had ended up being correct.
ghs.assessment: The narrator calls Kiri's earlier statement a prophecy that came true. 'Guess' removes its foretelling quality.

rows.jp: 人間なんて、アッサリ滅びてしまうものだ。
rows.en: Humanity could perish with astonishing ease.

ghs.en: Humans, indeed, perish so readily after all.
I quietly called out to her.
She turns around, taking her time.

rows.jp: 「……世界がこんなことになって……人もいなくなって……」
rows.en: “...The world has come to this... and everyone is gone...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...so the world came to be like this... where even people are gone..."

rows.jp: 「悪意はなくなったかわりに……密度もなくなって……」
rows.en: “The malice is gone... but so is the density...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "In exchange for malice being gone... its density is also gone..."
ghs.assessment: Kiri says that with malice gone, the density of the world or human existence has also vanished. The pronoun 'its' instead makes density a property of malice.
ghs.remedy: the density of life is gone too

rows.jp: 「それでも、あなたは変わらないんですね」

ghs.en: Kiri: "And yet there you are, unchanged."

rows.jp: 「……前から言おうと思っていました」
rows.en: “...I've been meaning to say this for a long time.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...I have meant to ask this for some time."

rows.jp: 「先輩はどうして、生きてるんですか？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Senpai, how come you are alive?"

rows.jp: 『なあ、ひとつ質問なんだけど……どうして今すぐにでも死なないんだ？』
rows.en: “Hey, one question... Why don't you just die right now?”

ghs.en: 『Say, I got one question though... why don't you just die right this very instant?』

rows.jp: まるで、昔投げつけた刃を、今になって不意に投げ返されたような。
rows.en: As if a blade I'd thrown long ago had suddenly been hurled back at me now.

ghs.en: Exactly as if the blade cast off long ago had now suddenly been thrown back at me.

rows.jp: 「自分に生きる資格があると思っているんですか？」
rows.en: “Do you believe you have the right to live?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Do you think you have the qualifications to live inside of yourself?"
ghs.assessment: Kiri asks whether he believes he has the right or qualification to live. The English invents the idea of living inside oneself.

highlights.text: the qualifications to live inside of yourself

rows.jp: 的確な比喩だと思った。

ghs.en: How the word uses that kanji from my last name. I found that to be an accurate metaphor.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese only says the narrator considers 'black' an apt metaphor. The English inserts an explicit explanation about the kanji in his surname.
ghs.remedy: I thought it was an apt metaphor.

highlights.text: How the word uses that kanji from my last name.

rows.jp: 「ヒトじゃない。ヒトに似たものでしかない。ヒトに擬態してる。虫みたいに」
rows.en: “You aren't human. You're only something that resembles one. You mimic humans. Like an insect.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "You're no person. You have nothing more than the semblance of a person. You camouflage yourself as a person. As insects do."

rows.jp: 「擬態して、ヒトに化けて、ヒトを襲う」
rows.en: “You mimic them, pass yourself off as human, and attack humans.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Camouflaged, you take the shape of a person, and attack people."

rows.jp: 「あなたは人を傷つけるものです。決して相容れない」
rows.en: “You are something that harms people. You can never coexist with us.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "You are something that hurts people. Completely incompatible."

rows.jp: 「どうしてあなたの適応係数が８０を越えているのか、昔は不思議でした。けどそれはまったくおかしなことじゃない。あなたの中のヒトの部分は、文字通り二割ほどしかない」
rows.en: “I used to wonder why your adaptation coefficient was over eighty. But there is nothing strange about it. The human part of you is literally only about twenty percent.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "The reason why your Conformity Coefficient crosses over 80 has been inexplicable to me for a long time. But that is absolutely nothing strange. Because the part inside you that is human is literally less than twenty percent and no more."

rows.jp: 今までたくわえられた佐倉霧という様式を覆す、鮮烈なイメージを構築していく。
rows.en: Building a vivid new image that overturned everything I had come to recognize as the Kiri Sakura pattern.

ghs.en: she goes to construct vivid images, overturning the pattern thus far preserved within the name Sakura Kiri.

rows.jp: 言葉のナイフが、俺の精神を刺そうとしていた。
rows.en: A knife of words sought to pierce my mind.

ghs.en: The knife that were those words were trying to stab at my very essence.
ghs.assessment: The English uses two incompatible finite verbs and fails subject-verb agreement.
ghs.remedy: The knife of her words was trying

highlights.text: The knife that were those words were trying

rows.jp: 今までは鈍い刃物しか持ち得なかった―――
rows.en: Until now, she had wielded only blunt blades—

ghs.en: The dull knife that was all she possessed so far---

rows.jp: 佐倉霧の切り札となって！
rows.en: Now they had become Kiri Sakura's trump card!

rows.jp: 「あなたの欺瞞は、怪物の分際で怪物に徹さないところです」
rows.en: “Your deceit is that, for a monster, you refuse to be a monster through and through.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Your deceit is that you do not pour your heart and soul into the monster you are, despite your place in society being that of a monster."

rows.jp: 「人と怪物との間に共感が芽生えて、仲良く幸せに暮らせると思っているんですか？　あなたが人並みの幸せを手に出来ると？」
rows.en: “Do you believe empathy can bloom between a human and a monster, and the two can live together happily ever after? That you can obtain the same happiness as any human?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Did you think that empathy could sprout between person and monster, and that you could have a happy life in harmony with others? That you would be able to lay hands on the happiness of the ordinary person?"

ghs.assessment: Kiri states that the imagined outcome is impossible. The English turns impossibility into a prediction that it will not occur.

rows.jp: 「世界にわずかしかない優しさは、決してあなたのために取り分けられない。いえ、取り分けられてはならないんです」
rows.en: “The scant kindness that exists in this world will never be set aside for you. No. It must not be set aside for you.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "In this world there is just a little kindness and no more, but there is absolutely no part set aside for you. No, it is simply out of the question that any ever would be set aside."

rows.jp: 「体を食い破って出てくる寄生虫に、愛を抱く人がいないのと一緒です。もしいたとしてもそれは狂人でしょう」
rows.en: “No one feels love for a parasite that tears its way out of their body. Anyone who did would be a madman.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "It is the same as no one would hug with love the parasite that comes out of their body, having devoured its way through it. Should one like that ever even exist, they would be madmen."
ghs.assessment: Kiri says no one would feel love for such a parasite. The English changes the feeling into a physical embrace.

rows.jp: 「あなたはいつも自分のために犠牲になってくれる獲物を捜してる。わたしにはわかります」
rows.en: “You're always searching for prey who will sacrifice themselves for you. I know.”

rows.jp: 「今まではそれは抑えられていた。けど世界がこんなことになって、ヒトの数が少なくなって、あなたの抑えはきかなくなってきてる」
rows.en: “Until now, you kept it in check. But now that the world has come to this and there are so few humans left, your restraint is starting to fail.”

rows.jp: 「擬態をする必要がなくなったからです」
rows.en: “Because you no longer need to mimic us.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Because the need for camouflage has vanished."

rows.jp: 「傷つけて楽しむため、あなたの目はいつも私たちに注がれている。それもひと思いにではなく、ゆっくりと時間をかけて嬲り尽くそうとしている」
rows.en: “Your eyes are always on us, so you can hurt us for pleasure. And not all at once—you mean to torment us slowly, taking all the time you need.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Your eyes are always focused on us, so that you can enjoy the hurting. And it's not something done instantly, you slowly take the time to perform that bullish sexual 'teasing' of yours all the way to the end."
ghs.assessment: Kiri accuses him of slowly tormenting people to exhaustion. The English invents both a bovine quality and a specifically sexual form of teasing.
ghs.remedy: torment them slowly to the bitter end

rows.jp: 「ヒトでもない、怪物でもない」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Not a person, nor a monster."

rows.jp: 「では何者なんですか？　何者でもないあなたこそ、世界から消えるべきだった。わたしはそう思います」
rows.en: “Then what are you? You, who are nothing at all, should have been the one to disappear from the world. That is what I believe.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Then who or what are you? You are neither who nor what, that is what you are, just something that ought to have disappeared from the world. That is what I think."

rows.jp: 「大半が悪意に満ちた人類だって、あなた一人の命よりはずっと価値があった。わたしにとってさえ、そうです」
rows.en: “Even a humanity filled mostly with malice had far more value than your single life. Even to me.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "The majority of mankind was so full of malice, but even that had a value far greater than your one life. To me, that is the truth."
Kiri: "I will give two pieces of advice."

rows.jp: 「まずあなたが他者との触れあいの中で本当の人間になれるのだと思っているとしたら、それは間違いです。あり得ません。人間を冒涜する考えです」
rows.en: “First, if you believe you can become truly human through contact with others, you are wrong. It is impossible. The very idea is an affront to humanity.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "The first, if you believe that within the exchange of touches with other people you will become a real human, you are mistaken. That will not be. Thinking that is to blaspheme humanity. Because I have never seen a more perfect monster than you, Senpai."

rows.jp: 「先輩ほど完璧なバケモノは見たことないですから」
rows.en: “Because I have never seen a monster as perfect as you.”

rows.jp: 「あなたは掛け値なしの精神異常者。狂人の中の狂人」
rows.en: “You are, without qualification, mentally deranged. A madman among madmen.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "You are, without exaggeration, a psychotic, a deviant of the soul. A madman among madmen."
Kiri: "...the crowning jewel of all that go mad."

rows.jp: 「そしてもう一つ。わたしたちに手を出そうとは思わないことです」
rows.en: “And second: do not think of laying a hand on any of us.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "And then one more. Do not even think of wanting to lay your hands on us in any sense."

rows.jp: 「もし先輩が生贄を求めてわたしたちに近づくことがあれば……」
rows.en: “If you ever approach us in search of a sacrifice...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Should you approach us in search for a sacrificial lamb, Senpai..."

rows.jp: 最後のひとつきを、霧は繰り出す。

ghs.en: Kiri unleashes the very final thrust.

rows.jp: 「……美希は絶対に、あなたには渡さない」
rows.en: “...I will never give Miki to you.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...I will never, ever hand Miki over to you."

rows.en: “I will not let you break her!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "I won't let you break her!"

rows.jp: つかつかと靴音を立てて、脇を通り過ぎる。
rows.en: Her shoes clicked briskly as she strode past me.

ghs.en: With the sound of determined footstep, she passes right underarm.
ghs.assessment: Kiri strides past the narrator's side. The English calques the body-part expression and says she passes beneath an armpit.

rows.en: A creaking door. A closing door.

rows.jp: 言葉を反芻して、噛みしめる。
rows.en: I turned the word over, chewing on it.

ghs.en: I ruminate over the word, and try biting into it.
ghs.assessment: The narrator turns the word over and absorbs its meaning. The English renders the idiom as a literal attempt to bite a word.
ghs.remedy: turn it over and take it in

ghs.en: That was something I know, yes, but.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says 'Even though I already knew it.' The English mixes past and present tense and leaves the concession malformed.
ghs.remedy: Even though I already knew it.

highlights.text: That was something I know, yes, but

rows.jp: 過去の記録通り、霧がやってくる。
rows.en: Just as the old record said, Kiri came.

ghs.en: Just as the records of the past said, Kiri came by.

rows.jp: まっすぐ、雑木林に入る。

ghs.en: Straight and forwards, into the grove of trees.

ghs.assessment: The narrator has one question or doubt. The English prematurely characterizes it as a problem.

rows.jp: 予定調和的に行動する人だろうか？
rows.en: Was she the sort of person who would play out a foreordained part?

ghs.en: Is she someone I should expect to act according to this harmonie preetabilie?
ghs.assessment: The Japanese asks whether Youko behaves according to a predetermined or scripted harmony. The English leaves the key concept as a misspelled, unexplained foreign phrase.

rows.jp: もし彼女が行動しなかったら。

ghs.en: Suppose the girl did not act:

rows.jp: 霧と俺との溝は、埋まるのか？
rows.en: Would the gulf between Kiri and me close?

ghs.en: would the gap between Kiri and me ever be filled?

rows.jp: 疑問を抱きつつ、目的の場所に。
rows.en: Still holding the question, I reached my destination.

ghs.en: While still holding on to the doubt, I come to the place that is my objective.

rows.en: I switched my eyes over in advance.

ghs.en: I switched my eyes in preparation.
I can see the night so clearly.
ghs.assessment: After changing his eyes, the night looks bright. The English changes brightness into visual clarity.

ghs.en: There was no semblance of surprise.

rows.jp: たぶん、知っていたのだろう。

rows.en: Kiri saw an opening and moved.

rows.jp: 起こりを突かれた霧には対処できない。
rows.en: Caught at the very start of her movement, Kiri could not respond.

ghs.en: Kiri, startled by the event, cannot deal with this.

rows.jp: ふくらはぎをしたたかに打つ。
rows.en: The stone struck her calf hard.

ghs.en: It strikes her calf with strength.

rows.jp: すとんとうずくまる霧。
足を抱えて、歯を食いしばる。激痛が走っているはずだ。
rows.en: She clutched her leg and gritted her teeth. The pain had to be excruciating.

ghs.en: Grasping her leg, grinding her teeth. She must be feeling intense pain.

rows.jp: 二つ目の石を、ベルトに挟む。
rows.en: She nestled a second stone in the sling.

ghs.en: She sets a second stone in the belt.

rows.jp: 手首のバネをきかせて、残像の円盤を作る。瞬時。
rows.en: A snap of her wrist spun the sling into a disc of afterimages. In an instant.

ghs.en: Utilizing the springiness in her wrist, she creates the afterimage of a disk. Instantly.

rows.en: The blood drained from Kiri's face.

ghs.en: Youko: "Because you want to kill Taichi."
ghs.assessment: Youko says Kiri tried to kill Taichi. The English changes the attempted act into a current desire.

rows.jp: 「太一を殺す練習をしていたから」
rows.en: “Because you were practicing how to kill Taichi.”

ghs.en: Youko: "Because you are practicing to kill Taichi."

rows.jp: 「……だ、だから……わたしを殺すんですか……？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...th-, that's why... you are going to kill me...?"

rows.jp: とにかく、考える時ではない。
rows.en: Whatever the answer, this was no time to think.

ghs.en: Regardless, this is not the time to think.

rows.jp: 予定通り行動するしかない。
rows.en: I could only act according to plan.

ghs.en: I can do no more than act as planned.

rows.en: A keen whistle through the air.

ghs.en: The sharp sound of wind cutting the air.

rows.jp: 眼前で膨れあがる破壊力、霧は恐怖に射竦(いすく)められる。
rows.en: The destructive force swelled before her eyes, pinning Kiri in place with fear.

ghs.en: As the destructive force swells out in front of her eyes, Kiri is bound down by fear.

rows.jp: それが霧には信じられない。

ghs.en: That is something that Kiri cannot believe.

rows.jp: 目の前で運動エネルギーがたくわえられていく。
rows.en: Kinetic energy was building before her eyes.

ghs.en: Kinetic energy is being stored right in front of her eyes.

rows.jp: クロスボウを顔の前に構えて、すすり泣いた。
rows.en: She held the crossbow in front of her face and sobbed.

ghs.en: Setting her crossbow in front of her face, she sobbed.

rows.en: I stepped in front of Kiri.

ghs.en: I stand in front of Kiri.

rows.jp: 「それは、生かしておくと太一に危害を加える」
rows.en: “If that stays alive, it'll hurt Taichi.”

ghs.en: Youko: "If that is kept alive then Taichi will be harmed."
Taichi: "Nah, I don't think so, not really."
ghs.assessment: Taichi accepts the risk and says it is fine if Kiri might harm him. The English instead denies Youko's claim that harm may occur.

highlights.text: Nah, I don't think so, not really

ghs.en: Taichi: "Lemme do what I wanna do."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says they should let Kiri do as she pleases. The English instead asks permission for Taichi himself to act freely.
ghs.remedy: Let's let her do as she pleases.

highlights.text: Lemme do what I wanna do

ghs.en: I call her name with strength,

rows.jp: けど引き下がる様子はない。
rows.en: But she showed no sign of backing down.

ghs.en: but it doesn't seem she's backing down.

rows.jp: それでも霧を殺す気なのか？
rows.en: Did she still intend to kill Kiri?

ghs.en: Does she still intend to kill Kiri after all this?

rows.jp: 背後で、霧が息を詰めて見守っている。
rows.en: Behind me, Kiri held her breath and watched.

ghs.en: Behind me, Kiri is holding her breath and watching attentively.

rows.jp: 命が助かった安堵と、俺に仲裁されたことへの違和。
rows.en: Relief that her life had been spared, mixed with unease at my intervention.

ghs.en: A physical discomfort towards the combination between the relief of her life being saved and the idea of my intercession.
ghs.assessment: Kiri feels emotional unease or dissonance at being saved through the narrator's intervention. The English changes this to bodily discomfort.

rows.jp: 「俺を理由にして、人殺しなんてしてもらいたくないね」
rows.en: “I don’t want you killing anyone on my account.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I don't want you to be a murderer using me as the reason."

rows.jp: 「殺したいなら自分の理由でやってくれ」
rows.en: “If you want to kill her, do it for your own reasons.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If you wanna kill, come up with a reason of your own."

rows.en: It might have been an act.

ghs.en: Perhaps it's acting, I don't know.
Youko: "......but, for the sake of Taichi... I..."

rows.jp: 俺の名前を出して霧を殺す。

ghs.en: Killing Kiri with my name on her lips.

rows.jp: そのことが、結果として俺を傷つけるとも考えず。
rows.en: Without considering that the result would hurt me.

ghs.en: And she'll do that without ever thinking if the result would hurt me.

rows.jp: 「……いつだってそうだ。自分の気持ちだけを押しつけて」
rows.en: “...You're always like this. Forcing your own feelings onto me.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...always, always like that. Always pushing onto others what are just your feelings."

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃんが手首をひねった。
横から首を出して会話をうかがっていた霧。
rows.en: Kiri had leaned her head out from behind me to listen to our exchange.

ghs.en: From the side, Kiri's head had poked out to peek into our conversation.

rows.jp: その顔面の前にてのひらを置く。
rows.en: I thrust my palm in front of her face.

ghs.en: I cover that face with the palm of my hand.
ghs.assessment: The narrator places his palm in front of Kiri's face to shield it. The English says he covers her face directly.
ghs.remedy: I put my palm in front of her face.

rows.jp: 石が当たるかと思ったが、外れて背後の幹を叩き割った。
rows.en: I thought the stone would find its mark, but it missed and split the trunk behind her.

ghs.en: I thought the stone would strike true, but it flies off and shatters the tree trunk behind us.

rows.en: Was it an act after all?

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃんが青ざめる。

rows.en: For an instant, I was confused.

ghs.en: She was confused for a moment,
ghs.assessment: The narrator is briefly confused, then proceeds according to plan. The English makes Youko the confused subject before switching back to the narrator in the next line.
ghs.remedy: I was confused for a moment

highlights.text: She was confused for a moment

rows.en: But I proceeded according to plan.

rows.jp: 「会話中に俺の隙を突こうとしたな」
rows.en: “You waited until we were talking and tried to catch me off guard.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You took advantage of me being distracted by conversation, didn't you."

rows.jp: びくっと、彼女の肩が震えた。
rows.en: Her shoulder gave a sudden twitch.

ghs.en: Her shoulders shook with a start.

rows.jp: 「大切だと言う。愛してると言う。好意を押しつける」
rows.en: “You say I'm precious. You say you love me. You force your affection on me.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You're precious, you tell me. I love you, you tell me. You keep pushing your favoritism on me."
ghs.assessment: Taichi accuses Youko of imposing her affection on him. Favoritism is preferential treatment and does not mean affection.

rows.jp: 「……なのに、ここぞという時に裏切る」
rows.en: “...And then betray me when it matters most.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...and despite all that, in those very critical moments, you betray me."

rows.jp: 「違う、それはつまり……太一の身の安全が……」

ghs.en: Youko: "Wrong, that was, I meant... to preserve Taichi's personal safety..."

rows.en: The words tangled on her tongue.

rows.jp: さすが、演技ともなると……うまいな。
rows.en: If this was an act... she was as good as I’d expect.

ghs.en: So like her, that even when it comes to acting performance... she's so good.

rows.jp: 二人で全部の役をやったんだもんな。
rows.en: The two of them had played every role between them, after all.

ghs.en: The two of us have played every role, indeed.

rows.jp: さあ、うまくやってくれよ。
rows.en: Now make this work for me.

ghs.en: Well then, let's do this right!
ghs.assessment: Internally, Taichi urges Youko to play her role well. The English turns this into a joint first-person proposal.
ghs.remedy: Now, play this well for me.

rows.jp: 一喝された幼女の如く、すくみあがった。
rows.en: She shrank like a little girl under a scolding.

ghs.en: She cowers in fright, like a little girl being shouted at.

rows.jp: 霧から武器と、抵抗する意志をごっそり奪って。
rows.en: Having stripped Kiri wholesale of both her weapon and her will to resist.

ghs.en: She forcibly and thoroughly stole weapons and volition to resist both from Kiri.

rows.jp: 背後、緊張の発生源がまだオーラを放出し続けている。
rows.en: Behind me, the source of that tension was still radiating its aura.

ghs.en: From behind, the source of tension continues to emit its aura.

rows.jp: ゆっくりと怒りに転化していくそれを意識しつつ、
rows.en: Aware that it was slowly transmuting into anger,

ghs.en: And while aware that it was slowly being converted into anger,

ghs.assessment: Kiri asks 'Why?' The English noun fragment is not a grammatical question.

rows.jp: 俺に助けられたことへの戸惑いや怒り。
rows.en: Confusion and anger at having been saved by me.

ghs.en: Angry and confused at having been saved by me.

rows.jp: 感情がもつれて、怒鳴りつけたいのを必死で抑えている。
rows.en: Her feelings tangled together as she fought desperately not to shout at me.

ghs.en: Emotions growing complicated, that she's holding back a desperate desire to scream.

rows.jp: そんなくぐもった声だった。
rows.en: Her voice came out muffled by the effort.

ghs.assessment: The Japanese concludes that this is what her muffled voice sounds like. The English instead begins an unfinished adjunct describing an action performed with the voice.
ghs.remedy: That was the quality of her muffled voice.

ghs.en: Kiri: "For what reason... did you save me..."

rows.jp: 「どうしてって……言われてもなぁ」
rows.en: “You ask me why... but I don't know what to tell you.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The reason you ask... don't got one."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says it is difficult to answer when asked why, then gives his reason in the next line. The English asserts that he has no reason at all.
ghs.remedy: Even if you ask me why...

rows.jp: 「助けたかったからそうした、じゃダメかな」
rows.en: “I saved you because I wanted to. Isn't that good enough?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I wanted to save you, that's it, is that a problem?"

rows.jp: 「ま、そうだよな。納得はいかんわな」
rows.en: “Well, you're right. I guess that would be hard to accept.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, that's how it goes. You're not gonna accept this anyway."

rows.jp: 「嫌っていた相手に助けられるというのは」

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's what being rescued by someone you don't like is about."
ghs.assessment: Taichi describes being rescued by someone Kiri hated. 'Don't like' substantially weakens that hostility.

rows.jp: 「本気で俺のこと、殺す気だったの？」
rows.en: “Did you truly mean to kill me?”

「こっちもいくぞー！　こら、こっちがレシーブしたらそっちの攻撃権はナシ」
rows.en: “Our turn! Hey, once we receive, you lose your attack rights.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'm gonna get going tooo! Come on, if I make a receive you lose the right to attack!"

rows.jp: 「レシーブしたら、相手の捕球に対してこっちが攻撃じゃ！　せやー！　一掃～！」
rows.en: “After a receive, we get to attack while the other side catches! Hyaa! Sweep!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Once I receive, I will be attacking whoever goes to make the catch! Sh'yah! Clean swee～ep!"

rows.jp: 「きゃっ、ちょっと先輩！　そういう雨っぽい水じゃ有効打として認めれないですよ」
rows.en: “Eek! Wait, Kurosu! Water sprayed like rain doesn’t count as a valid hit.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Kyah, wait Senpai! We cannot accept that rain-like drizzle as a proper attack!"
Taichi: "Mgh... battery wore out... I guess?"

rows.jp: 「ふっふっふー、こっちは交互に撃ってたからまだまだ攻撃できますもん！」
rows.en: “Heh-heh-heh! We took turns shooting, so we've still got plenty of attacks left!”

ghs.en: Miki: "Heh heh heeeh, we have been firing in alternation, so we still got lots and lots of attack power left!"

rows.jp: 「……えーい、そのくらいのハンデは納得済みだー！」
rows.en: “...Bah! I accepted that much of a handicap from the start!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...yeee-es, that I would've that handicap I've known aaall along!"

rows.jp: 「攻撃できなくても、純粋にバレーだけで十分だね！」
rows.en: “Even if I can't attack, pure volleyball is all I need!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If I can't attack, then pure volleyball alone will be enough!"

rows.jp: 「うん、すっごく強気。いっつもそう」
rows.en: “Yeah. Incredibly bold. He's always like that.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Yep, waaay cocksure. Alllway like this."
Kiri: "But that's just bravado isn't it."
Miki: "Yep, just an ostentatious show-off he is."

rows.jp: 「こらー、本人を前にして陰口叩くなー！」
rows.en: “Hey! Don't gossip about me right in front of my face!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Come ooon, don't talk smack about someone in front of theeem!"

rows.jp: ビーチバレーとサバゲーを組み合わせた高度な遊びを、俺たちは楽しんだ。
rows.en: We enjoyed an advanced game combining beach volleyball with a survival game.

ghs.en: We enjoyed playing of a High-Level combination of beach volley and survival game.
